functions.name: split
functions.signature: template <typename V, typename Extractor, typename K = typename std::invoke_result_t<Extractor, V const&>> std::map<K, std::vector<V>> split(std::vector<V> const& data, Extractor extractor)
functions.description: Groups elements of the input vector by a key extracted from each element. For each element v in data, extractor(v) is computed to obtain a key K, and v is appended to the vector at r[key] in the returned std::map. Typical usage: provide a vector of values and a callable (lambda, function object, or function pointer) that takes const V& and returns a key; the function returns a map from each key to the vector of corresponding elements. Notes: the input is not modified; elements are copied into the output vectors; ordering of keys follows std::map ordering; requires C++17 for std::invoke_result_t.
requirements: data must be a valid std::vector<V> whose elements are CopyInsertable into std::vector<V> (elements are copied into the result).
extractor must be invocable with signature compatible with K(V const&) and must be callable for every element in data.

The deduced key type K must be suitable as a key in std::map with the default comparator (i.e., supports a strict-weak-ordering via operator< compatible with std::less<K>) and be copy/move insertable.
The function requires C++17 or later (uses std::invoke_result_t).
Exceptions may propagate from extractor, from copying/moving V or K, and from allocations performed by std::map/std::vector.
